name: Datum Mesh
tagline: One open-source platform for structural and finite-element analysis: frames, plates, solids, heat and vibration, our own solver that proves its answers.
for: Mechanical, structural, process and aerospace engineers, students and lecturers.
about: Its purpose: to show any engineer or student how a part or structure carries load, heat and vibration (where it is stressed, how far it moves, how hot it gets) in a free app they can trust because it proves its own answers.

From 0.9.1 the window is laid out for the work: the steps down the left (Geometry, Materials, Loads, Mesh, Solve, Results, each ticked when done), the model across the middle, a card that pops up when you pick something, and a terminal along the bottom that keeps every message and follows each solve as it runs (increments, iterations, how far from balance, cut-backs, time left, Stop). It has full sketching and 3D modelling: click a plane and the view turns to it; lines, arcs, circles and rectangles drawn several ways, polygons, slots, ellipses, splines, trim, offset, fillet, mirror, patterns, dimensions and constraints; extrude with the solid changing as you type, revolve, boxes, cylinders, cones and spheres made in one go, solids joined, cut or intersected, sweeps, lofts, drafts and splits, STEP files in and out, holes, fillets, chamfers, shells, press pull, move, mirror and patterns of solids; frames drawn with the same sketch tools, and a history of every feature to edit, suppress, roll back or delete. The solids are then meshed by Gmsh (installed with it) and analysed by Datum Mesh's own engine, with supports and loads on the faces you click. The geometry comes from SolidCraft's open-source engine, working behind the Datum window.

Datum Mesh finds the stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and structures by the finite-element method. You draw a frame of beams and truss bars, or the outline of a part with its holes, put on the supports and loads, and solve.

Frames and trusses give the deflected shape, the moment, shear and axial diagrams, the reactions and member utilisation, by linear analysis or in steps with large deflection and P-delta, followed past the limit load, in 2D and 3D; 3D frames carry plates (slabs, walls) joined to their beams; frames and plates respond to earthquakes by response spectrum or time history. Parts are meshed into triangles and solved in plane stress, plane strain or steady heat conduction, or as 3D solids (extruded or revolved) for stress, vibration and heat, and elastic-plastic (yielding) up to collapse in both; 3D solids also follow large deformation, rubber included (with thermal stress from the temperatures), with contours of stress, displacement, safety factor and temperature, and a probe that reads any point. Every solve ends with an equilibrium check, and Help › Verification solves benchmarks with known answers in front of you (a plate with a hole, a thick cylinder, NAFEMS LE1, conduction, patch tests, the NAFEMS large-deflection beams, the Scordelis–Lo roof and the pinched cylinder), so you can see how far to trust each result.

steps.title: Geometry
steps.text: Click a plane or a face and the view turns to it; draw with lines, arcs, circles, rectangles, polygons and slots, size them with dimensions and constraints; Finish, and the shape is extruded as you set the distance. Revolve, drill, round and shell; edit any step in the history.

steps.title: Properties
steps.text: Pick the material from the library.

steps.title: Supports & Loads
steps.text: Click faces of the solid to hold them (fixed, roller, symmetry) or to load them (force, pressure).

steps.title: Mesh
steps.text: Meshed by itself when you need it: Gmsh fills the solids with ten-node tetrahedra; set the element size if you like.

steps.title: Solve
steps.text: Datum Mesh's own engine solves and checks that the reactions balance the loads.

steps.title: Results
steps.text: Von Mises stress or movement in colour bands on the deformed part, with a legend.

highlights: Four starting points: 2D frame, 3D frame, 2D part and 3D solid
Frames: point and part-length loads, split, reverse and merge, member orientation, a model check, loads and assignments tables, and combinations by rule with your own factors
Mesh statistics, solver settings and status badges that keep the model, the solve and the balance apart
Standard parts (bolts, nuts, washers, pins), the origin with show/hide eyes, and a see-through view cube
A terminal along the bottom: every edit, message and solve kept with its time, and a solver monitor that shows each load increment and iteration as it runs, with Stop
Impact: fast events in a meshed solid stepped in time (explicit dynamics), with starting velocities, the movement and energies in time, and a stress wave checked against its exact answer
Contact between solids: touching parts press on each other and slide, held back by friction, with the contact pressure and forces shown; checked against exact answers in benchmark 36
Remote forces and moments carried onto a face, a finer mesh near the faces you choose, and results graphed along a line through the solid
Sweep, loft, draft, split and measure; STEP files in and out; buildings laid out by levels and a column grid, with slabs drawn as plates

3D frames drawn as they will be built: each member shown as its I, channel, angle, box or tube section, turned the way the solver turns it; boxes, cylinders, cones and spheres made in one go and combined

roadmap.title: Design foundations
items: Design members from a chain of members, with restraints and segments
Values at any point along a member; section properties
Mechanics checks: stress, Euler buckling, deflection and storey drift, with the working shown and what was not checked

roadmap.title: Geometry tools
items: Datum planes, axes and points; split a face; overlaps and exploded view
Sketch: project edges, tangent arcs, driven dimensions; repairing imported STEP

roadmap.title: Filling in the map
items: Results tools, materials, setup (releases, links, springs, damping), more analyses
Hexahedra, refinement by itself, job queue and Python

roadmap.title: Complete
items: Design checks to a standard that is free to use
